title: Chorus Span Timeline Drill Visualizer
creator: Leah Patel
description: Design a compact, multi-trace visualization (the "Chorus") for Redwood Console that surfaces aligned span timelines across correlated requests. The Chorus view helps operators and engineers quickly spot systemic latency/cost patterns, understand which rollout/model-variant served which span, and jump into individual trace detail. This ticket covers interaction patterns, visual encoding for latency/cost/throughput, filter and correlation controls, lightweight prototyping for user testing, and engineering handoff notes.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates aligned multi-trace timeline for a selected correlation ID with at least 8 aligned spans visible across requests
UI shows per-span cost and latency overlays, and allows toggling cost/latency layers
Filter bar supports: time range, service name, span name, model-variant tag, rollout group, error status
Ability to click a chorus row to open the canonical trace detail in the existing Trace Inspector
Performance target: rendering of aggregated chorus (up to 200 requests) under 500ms on a mid-range laptop (prototype measurement)
Design specs and Figma prototype uploaded and labeled for front-end implementation
design_notes: Primary metaphor: 'chorus' — horizontally aligned sequences where each lane is a request and vertical alignment is span identity/operation
Row compaction: stack similar-duration spans into condensed glyphs to avoid vertical overflow; allow expand/collapse per-request
Encoding: latency uses width (ms) and heat tint; cost uses a thin sparkline overlay or hatch pattern when enabled
Rollout/model-variant integration: small badge on span representing variant id; hover reveals the rollout bucket and rollout percentage
Correlation stitching: show a breadcrumb of upstream correlation IDs when traces fork; present primary correlation ID prominently
Interaction: keyboard jump (J/K) to next/previous span, space to focus, Enter to open trace inspector; tooltips include links to GitHub PR or deploy tag if present
Filtering priority: keep filter bar lightweight — frequently used filters (service, span, variant, error) visible; advanced filters in an overflow panel
Accessibility: ensure 6:1 contrast for heat colors; provide alt text for exported PNG snapshots
Export: allow quick export of selected chorus as JSON snapshot for postmortem attachments
decisions: Use server-side pre-aggregation for chorus buckets to avoid fetching full traces for the default view
Limit default chorus to top 100 correlated requests by request frequency; allow user override to 200
Render timeline using an HTML5 Canvas layer for performance, with SVG overlays for interactive badges
Cost overlay is optional by default to reduce visual noise; enabled in two-clicks from the filter bar
Prototype will use synthetic dataset anonymized from Sandbox traces — real customer data not used in initial testing
